items.title: Impossible to configure_docker, since container_registry_domains is not stored when --use-keyring is supplied and also not checked
items.body:
### Checklist

<!-- Please test the latest versions, that will remove the possibility that you see a bug that is fixed in a newer version. -->

- [x] I'm using the latest version of the extension (Run `glab --version`)
  - Extension version: 1.65.0
- [x] Operating system and version: Fedora 42
- [x] Gitlab.com or self-managed instance? self-managed instance
- [x] GitLab version (if self-managed) 18.05
- [x] I have performed `glab auth status` to check for authentication issues
- [ ] Run the command in debug mode (like `DEBUG=true glab mr list`) and attach any useful output

### Summary

Using `glab auth login` with `--use-keyring` does not store the survey answer to supplied container registry domains.

Additionally `glab auth status` does not check for validity of container registry credentials.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Login with `glab auth login --use-keyring` and provide container registry domains
2. Try to do `glab auth configure-docker`
3. See the error

### What is the current _bug_ behavior?

The error is thrown:

```
ERROR: no hosts were configured - ensure you've logged in via oauth2 and configured at least one container registry domain for a host
```

### What is the expected _correct_ behavior?

`configure_docker` succeeds and container registry domains are retained when using the keyring, as without using `--use-keyring`.

Else the error could also be more understandable, such as "no container registries found in configuration retrieved from keyring/configuration file at path …".

items.title: Share one ID-parsing helper through cmdutils so invalid-ID errors name the rejected value
items.body:
## Summary

Eighteen commands print a bare `strconv` error when an ID argument is not a number, with no indication of which argument was wrong:

```shell
$ glab runner-controller get abc

   ERROR

  strconv.ParseInt: parsing "abc": invalid syntax.
```

Each of those commands already passes a usable description, and it is discarded. `cmdutils.WrapError(err, "invalid runner controller ID")` stores that string in `ExitError.Details`, but `ExitError.Error()` (`internal/cmdutils/errors.go:91`) returns only the wrapped error, so the detail never reaches the user. The parameter is in fact named `log` rather than `details` (`errors.go:80`), which is a fair account of what the field was originally for.

`Details` has no live reader anywhere in the CLI. The only production reader is `internal/commands/update/check_update.go:350`, and it cannot fire: it sits in `PrintUpdateError`, which is reached only from `cmd/glab/main.go`, and `internal/commands/update` contains no `WrapError` or `CancelError` call site, so no `*ExitError` ever arrives there. The only other production reader of `*ExitError` is `main.go`, which uses it solely to choose the exit code. So roughly 180 call sites populate a field nothing renders: 162 `WrapError`, 7 `WrapErrorWithCode` and 14 `CancelError`.

How the message reaches the terminal: `fang.DefaultErrorHandler` (`vendor/charm.land/fang/v2/help.go:111`) calls `err.Error()` only, never walking `Unwrap`, and appends a literal `.`. Fang also title-cases the entire first word through `titleFirstWord` (`vendor/charm.land/fang/v2/theme.go:202`), which rewrote `strconv.ParseInt` to `Strconv.parseint` and `POST` to `Post`, but !4141 turned that off with `styles.ErrorText.UnsetTransform()`, so error text now renders as written. There is consequently no constraint on where in a message a user-supplied value may sit. One consequence inside this issue's own scope: the `deploy-token get` workaround was written against the old behaviour and its comment still cites it, so that comment is now obsolete on two counts and should go with the migration.

Affected packages: `internal/commands/runnercontroller`, with 12 messages across 10 files because `token/revoke` and `token/rotate` each parse two IDs, and `internal/commands/runner`, with 6.

## Scope

Numeric parsing of user-supplied arguments across `internal/commands/` falls into six shapes:

| Shape | Sites | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `WrapError` with a detail that never names the value | 18 | `runnercontroller/get/get.go:69` |
| Names the value in the wrapped error | 18 | `deploy-token/get/get.go:87` |
| `cmdutils.FlagError` | 1 | `todo/done/done.go:67` |
| Returns the raw `strconv` error unwrapped | 8 | `milestone/delete/delete.go:63` |
| `utils.StringToInt`, which reports no error at all | 8 | `gpg-key/get/get.go:61` |
| Parse failure is deliberate control flow | 19 | `token/revoke/revoke.go:91` |

The first row is the reported problem. The second row is the same problem already solved 18 times in three different wordings: `"<thing> ID must be a valid integer, got %q"` under `cluster/agent`, `"<thing> ID must be an integer: %s"` under `deploy-key`, `packages` and `securefile`, and `"invalid <thing> ID %q"` under `mr/note` and `deploy-token`. Only `deploy-token/get` keeps `WrapError` alongside it; the other 17 drop it for a bare `fmt.Errorf`.

**The last row must not be touched.** Those 19 sites use a failed parse as a branch rather than an error, so a sweep that "fixes" them changes behaviour. `token/revoke/revoke.go:91` is the clearest case: a non-numeric argument there means the user passed a token name, not a bad ID.

## Proposal

A helper for this already exists, in a command package rather than a shared one: `internal/commands/container_registry/registryutils/registryutils.go:17`, with five callers. It names the argument's role but not the rejected value, and discards the `strconv` error.

Promote it into `cmdutils` and have it name the value:

```go
func ParseID(value, name string) (int64, error) {
	id, err := strconv.ParseInt(value, 10, 64)
	if err != nil || id < 1 {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("invalid %s: %q", name, value)
	}

	return id, nil
}
```

A caller then writes `cmdutils.ParseID(args[0], "runner controller ID")` and the user sees `invalid runner controller ID: "abc".` The value goes last because the sentence reads better that way, not because of any rendering constraint.

Then migrate the 18 sites in the first row, the 18 in the second, and the 5 existing `registryutils` callers, which settles the three competing wordings at the same time. The `runner` and `runnercontroller` sites are the ones that change user-visible behaviour; the rest is consolidation.

One behaviour change to decide explicitly rather than inherit: the existing helper rejects `id < 1`, so migrated sites would start rejecting `0` and negative IDs locally instead of sending them to the API. That looks right, since no GitLab resource has ID 0, but it is a change and should be a deliberate choice.

## Why not render `Details` as a prefix

Making `ExitError.Error()` return `Details + ": " + Err` was the first idea, and it is tempting because it fixes all 18 sites without touching them. It has problems that outweigh that:

- It double-prefixes every site in the second row, including the one that prompted this issue, which would read `invalid deploy token ID: invalid deploy token ID: "not-a-number"`. Those 18 sites need editing either way, so the saving does not apply where the problem actually is.
- It silently disables the usage hint. `isUsageError` (`vendor/charm.land/fang/v2/help.go:136`) decides whether to print "Try `--help` for usage." with `strings.HasPrefix(err.Error(), ...)` against `"invalid argument"`, `"unknown flag:"` and three others. Any usage error wrapped in an `ExitError` stops matching and loses its hint.
- It changes the machine-readable contract, not only stderr. `PrintJSONError` (`internal/iostreams/print_json.go:50`) fills `{"error":{"message":...}}` from `err.Error()`, so every scripted consumer sees the new text too.
- Many detail strings were never written to be read by anyone. `"prompting for SSH key to delete."`, `"Retrieving list of SSH keys."` and `"could not prompt"` would render as `Prompting for SSH key to delete.: EOF`. Doing this properly means auditing all ~180.
- `internal/commands/df/dfcmd/dfcmd.go:122` and `:126` pass `ee.Error()` itself as the detail, which already contains the unwrapped text, so the result is `failed to run npm: exit status 1: exit status 1`.
- `TestNewGitLabErrorHandler_JSONOutput_ExitErrorOmitsLogDetail` (`internal/cmdutils/errors_test.go:66`) pins the current behaviour as a decision, not incidentally: its comment says the JSON envelope deliberately mirrors `Error()`'s contract rather than surfacing the log text.

Worth stating plainly so it is not re-litigated on the wrong grounds: test fallout is **not** the objection. Only about 13 assertions break, because nearly every test uses `Contains` on the error rather than an exact match.

## Out of scope

Two separable items found while scoping this, each worth its own issue rather than being folded in here:

- **`Details` is dead weight.** Around 180 call sites populate it and nothing reads it. It should either be rendered somewhere deliberately or removed, and the same question applies to `Code`, which is carried on the struct but absent from the JSON envelope. The envelope was built for this: the comment above `jsonErrorEnvelope` says it is nested so that fields can be added later without changing the type of an existing one.
- **`utils.StringToInt` discards its error.** `internal/utils/utils.go:291` returns `0` on a parse failure, so the 8 commands in the fifth row above silently act on ID 0. `glab gpg-key get abc` requests key 0 rather than reporting a bad argument. That is a behaviour bug, not a message one.

items.title: Add merge_after to gl mr create/update
items.body:
<!---
Please read this!

Before opening a new issue, make sure to search for keywords in the issues
filtered by the "feature" label:

 - https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/issues/?label_name%5B%5D=type%3A%3Afeature

and verify the issue you're about to submit isn't a duplicate.
--->

### Problem to solve

- Be on-par with API and UI.
- Merge-after is especially useful for automated merges, which glab would be used for.

### Proposal

glab mr create/update does not support the merge_after flag (https://docs.gitlab.com/api/merge_requests/#create-mr).

### Further details

<!--Include examples, use cases, benefits, goals, or any other details that will help us understand the problem better.-->

### Links / references

https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/510992

<!-- implementation plan added during 2026-09 backlog triage -->

## Implementation plan

> **Note:** This plan was drafted during an AI-assisted triage of the backlog and has not been validated by a maintainer. Treat it as a starting point: file paths, line numbers, and the approach may need adjusting.

The REST API accepts `merge_after` on both Create MR and Update MR since GitLab 17.8, but `client-go` v3.13.0 does not model it in the option structs glab passes, so the first step is upstream.

1. **Add the field upstream in `client-go`.** In `gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go`, add `MergeAfter *time.Time` with the tags `url:"merge_after,omitempty" json:"merge_after,omitempty"` to both `CreateMergeRequestOptions` and `UpdateMergeRequestOptions` in `merge_requests.go`. `ListIssuesOptions` in `issues.go` is the tag pattern to copy. Once that release is out, bump `gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go/v3` in glab's `go.mod` and run `go mod vendor`.
2. **Add the flag to `glab mr create`.** In `internal/commands/mr/create/mr_create.go`, add a `mergeAfter time.Time` field to `options`, register the flag next to the other create flags with `mrCreateCmd.Flags().TimeVar(&opts.mergeAfter, "merge-after", time.Time{}, []string{time.RFC3339}, "...")`, copying the pattern at `internal/commands/mr/list/mr_list.go:144`, and set `mrCreateOpts.MergeAfter` in `run` (the struct is built at `mr_create.go:376`) only when `cmd.Flags().Changed("merge-after")` is true. `TimeVar` handles parsing and the invalid-format error, so no hand-rolled `time.Parse` is needed.
3. **Add the flag to `glab mr update`.** Same flag registration in `internal/commands/mr/update/mr_update.go` near the other flag definitions, and set `l.MergeAfter` on the `gitlab.UpdateMergeRequestOptions` built at `mr_update.go:130`, guarded on `Changed("merge-after")`. Add the value to the action list the command prints so the output reports what changed.
4. **Tests.** Extend `internal/commands/mr/create/mr_create_test.go` and `internal/commands/mr/update/mr_update_test.go`. Use the existing `cmdtest` setup in those files and assert on the request body the `httpmock` stub receives, so the test proves `merge_after` reaches the API, plus one case asserting the error message for a non-RFC3339 value.
5. **Docs.** Run `make gen-docs` and commit the regenerated `docs/source/mr/create.md` and `docs/source/mr/update.md` in the same commit. Do not edit those files by hand.

Prior attempt: merge request !2767 added the flag by hand-rolling `CreateMR`/`UpdateMRWithMergeAfter` wrappers in `internal/api/merge_request.go` to work around the missing `client-go` field. That MR was closed as stale. Fixing `client-go` first avoids the duplicate API layer.
